pr_title: Load user rulesets from the game data directory
pr_body:
# Summary

This allows storing the user rulesets under the rulesets folder in the game data directory (as an interim fix in the wait for rulesets to get databased) and get them picked up by the `RulesetStore` (`loadUserRulesets()`).

The runtime won't be able to load dependencies for assemblies located outside of the executable directory, thus manual referencing to the game core assembly using .NET Standard AppDomain resolution mechanism has been added to `RulesetStore`
This assumes the only dependency custom rulesets have is on the game core, other transitive assembly references (framework) are resolved automatically by the runtime from the resolved game core assembly.

# Remarks

While messing with AppDomain assembly resolution in `RulesetStore`, I stumbled upon this line which I fail to understand its effect.

```csharp
private Assembly resolveRulesetAssembly(object sender, ResolveEventArgs args) => loadedAssemblies.Keys.FirstOrDefault(a => a.FullName == args.Name);
```

After testing without this line, I can confirm everything still works fine. So I suppose it is fine to remove that line as I did (unless I missed something on the reason of existence for this line?)


No automated tests for this as it is quite hard to automatically test this.
I tested the behaviour on my machine with the tau ruleset and can confirm it works.

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/8545

issue_context.title: Add the ability to transfer custom rullsets when updating the application
issue_context.body:
When updating, they are not saved and are in the folder with the old patch

**Proposal designs of the feature:** 
I think that in the settings you can add a transfer button. Or enable automatic transfer
comments: One way to tackle this would be to create a Rulesets folder in the game data directory where the custom Rulesets assemblies are put and so aren't located at a path dependent of the game version. Or to have Rulesets databased like every other game content.
or the other selection is by overwriting the file when restarting the game.

Storing to the database may be the final goal, but for now I believe a `rulesets` folder is best (as we may be changing database engine in the near future and are avoiding making any large database changes).

review_comments: it looks like this was here to cache assembly lookups. have you checked what happens (or even if it happens) when a ruleset assembly is resolved the second time?

Ah, This makes sense now. 
However, after testing on master, this line doesn't have any effect effect because the event handler is attached after actual the assembly lookup is done (the event is never raised)
As of having a ruleset assembly being resolved twice; I don't have any scenario in mind where this could happen (apart from loading the same ruleset assembly but with different filenames, 
which is handled by the ruleset store)? Looks like I'm missing something.
I'm not sure myself, but the first thing i'd do is git blame and see if there are any hints.

After looking at the class commit log, that was added back in f2a9e95d.
Gonna add the loaded assembly lookup back as it seems to allow resolving assemblies without having full assembly info matching.
As I commented before, is there a reason why this is done in the specific place it's being done here? Rather than at the bottom where it was initially?

The event handler contains code for resolving dependency on the game assembly for Rulesets located outside the base game directory. 

It needs to be attached  to the lookup event before the actual call to `loadUserRulesets()` else Rulesets located out the base game directory will fail to load as unable to locate the game assemblies.

 (should've made it clear from the start .... sorry)
Maybe could have a comment here why this needs to be before the user ruleset load?
does this create the directory automatically?
ah yes, it does, all good.
